The method `org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars)` checks if any of the characters in the given character sequence `cs` are contained in the provided array of characters `searchChars`. It iterates through each character in `cs` and compares it with each character in `searchChars`.

The issue reported states that the StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly. In this case, the failing test `testContainsAnyCharArrayWithSupplementaryChars` attempts to test the behavior with Unicode supplementary characters U+20000 and U+20001.

Looking at the implementation of `containsAny`, it checks for equality between characters using `searchChars[j] == ch`. However, this comparison may not work correctly for Unicode supplementary characters, as they require special handling due to their representation in UTF-16.

To handle Unicode supplementary characters correctly, the comparison logic in `containsAny` needs to be updated to properly compare and handle supplementary characters.

Next, I will identify the method that needs to be fixed to address this issue.
